questions.enonce_markdown: Draw the truth table for each of the propositions $p \Longrightarrow q$ and $\sim p \vee q$ and show that they are identical. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two propositions are logically equivalent (identical) when they have the same truth value for every assignment of truth values to $p$ and $q$. There are $2^2 = 4$ assignments. Recall that $p \Longrightarrow q$ is false only when $p$ is true and $q$ is false, and that $\sim p \vee q$ means $(\sim p) \vee q$.

| $p$ | $q$ | $p \Longrightarrow q$ | $\sim p$ | $\sim p \vee q$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | T | T | F | T |
| T | F | F | F | F |
| F | T | T | T | T |
| F | F | T | T | T |

The column for $p \Longrightarrow q$ (T, F, T, T) is identical to the column for $\sim p \vee q$ (T, F, T, T) in every row. Hence
$$\boxed{p \Longrightarrow q \;\equiv\; \sim p \vee q}$$
the two propositions are identical. $\blacksquare$

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $\sin^{-1}(x) = \alpha$ and $\cos^{-1}(x) = \beta$ show that $\sin(\alpha + \beta) = 1$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Both inverse functions are defined for $-1 \le x \le 1$. From the definitions,
$$\sin\alpha = x, \qquad \cos\beta = x,$$
with $\alpha \in \left[-\tfrac{\pi}{2}, \tfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ and $\beta \in [0, \pi]$ (principal values).

**Find the other two ratios.**
- On $\left[-\tfrac{\pi}{2}, \tfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$, $\cos\alpha \ge 0$, so $\cos\alpha = +\sqrt{1 - \sin^2\alpha} = \sqrt{1 - x^2}$.
- On $[0, \pi]$, $\sin\beta \ge 0$, so $\sin\beta = +\sqrt{1 - \cos^2\beta} = \sqrt{1 - x^2}$.

**Apply the addition formula** $\sin(\alpha + \beta) = \sin\alpha\cos\beta + \cos\alpha\sin\beta$:
$$\sin(\alpha + \beta) = x \cdot x + \sqrt{1 - x^2}\cdot\sqrt{1 - x^2} = x^2 + (1 - x^2) = 1. \qquad \blacksquare$$

(Consequence: $\alpha + \beta = \tfrac{\pi}{2}$, i.e. $\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x = \tfrac{\pi}{2}$, because $\alpha + \beta \in [-\tfrac\pi2, \tfrac{3\pi}{2}]$ and the only angle there with sine $1$ is $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$.)
